evidence:
The required empirical app-ranking evidence is absent; the source arithmetic is monotone. Inspected the actual frozen XLSX with openpyxl: Quality Checks!row 43 (check 42) states "A worse app never outscores a better one ? weights/gates/criteria don't invert the ranking"; Internal Quality Checks!row 43 says "Mukesh - we need to monitor this one." Applied the frozen Harbor SKILL.md, quality-checks.md:172-173, staged-task-contract.md:tests/scoring.toml and deterministic-checks.md:40-42. qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md:31 requires separate hash-bound runtime records for reward ordering; the frozen skill explicitly says never upgrade an unmeasured claim to Pass.

Source review covered all five complete judge TOMLs, all five prompts, shared app context, public brief/six notes, scorer and test.sh. Under .qc-cache/coldwater-2026-09-30-postrepair-audit/task/, tests/scoring.toml:1-11 has zero-weight Render/Constraints gates, positive Functional/Polish/Visual shares 0.6/0.2/0.2, and Functional floor 0.05. All criterion weights are positive: 64 Functional binary outcomes sum to 32.7, 7 Polish outcomes sum to 4.0, 6 Visual Likert outcomes sum to 6.0, and each gate has one binary outcome. tests/tools/score.py:41-48 uses gates_passed=all(score>floor), weighted positive arithmetic mean, floors_passed=all(score>floor), and reward=round(weighted,4) only after passing both. This is coordinatewise nondecreasing, including the floor discontinuity. tests/scored/visual/prompt.md:39-42 explicitly uses (raw-1)/4. Functional carries more total mass than both craft dimensions combined. The frozen test.sh and score.py were byte-compared to the frozen canonical template and are identical.

Read-only synthetic execution used the unmodified score.py main() via runpy, replacing only its log-directory Path with an in-memory filesystem, while retaining the actual policy file. Tested every 5-dimensional score tuple from [0,0.01,0.05,0.050001,0.1,0.5,1]: 16,807 states and 72,030 single-coordinate upward steps, with zero reward decreases. With both gates passing and Polish=Visual=1, Functional 0/0.05/0.050001/0.5/1 produced rewards 0/0/0.43/0.7/1. A failing Constraints gate with all scored dimensions 1 produced zero. These are scorer measurements, not judge-generated app scores, and do not establish that the judge maps product quality monotonically into these inputs.

Conforming-alternative challenge: a plain/native-looking app with server-rendered library data, different control labels, proactive stale-Save prevention and a static rollback snapshot remains eligible. Constraints judge.toml:27 accepts server-rendered records and says "Do not require a separate JSON/list endpoint"; Render judge.toml:27 grades "only this ordinary successful run"; app_context.md:12 accepts proactive prevention and no prescribed recovery control; app_context.md:18 allows a static restored snapshot; Visual judge.toml's described top anchors accept native/simple styling. Thus these plausible conforming differences did not expose a stronger-app gate penalty in the written rules. App-context line 16 also prevents missing Auto-run alone from zeroing unrelated gates. Functional prompt:97-107 preserves independent outcome observations, with explicit fallbacks at 143-145, 220, 265, 370, 413 and 425.

Broken-app challenge: static output/localStorage-only persistence cannot satisfy the authored-run and independent-clean-context save/read gates. A separate inherited restart weakness remains relevant to possible overcredit: tests/test.sh:154-159 sends only TERM and waits without requiring the old process to exit; lines 172-183 accept any successful HTTP listener as a completed restart. The hash-bound raw inherited-restart-counterexample.json records helper_returncode=0, old_pid=7, claimed_new_pid=67, old_still_running=true, before.pid=after.pid=7 and an EADDRINUSE error for the new process. I read reproduce_restart.py itself: it constructs a process with process.on('SIGTERM',()=>{}), extracts the current canonical helper, executes it, checks the still-running old process and captures the log. This confirms the restart false-success primitive, not an observed full-app reward inversion. No new Docker run was performed.

Evidence binding: recomputed every frozen task and rules file hash against manifest.json, with no mismatches; current review-policy hash also matches. Recomputed the three raw-artifact SHA256 values from raw-evidence-index.json, all matching. Parsed golden RESULTS.json and verified all listed golden app hashes plus Functional judge/prompt hashes against frozen bytes. Its metadata says browser_driver="direct pinned Playwright", case="golden", wall_seconds=118.82740359200398, oracle_score_claimed=false; its pre.scope says "no LLM/provider/platform execution", and surface.visual_grade_measured=false. Those logs supply product observations for one reference app, not score ordering of stronger/weaker implementations. The current run contains no runtime-evidence.json, and the raw index explicitly states no full configured verifier, target model, Oracle or measured judge workload. No supplied app-pair judge rewards establish this row. Therefore this is PARTIAL source/scorer verification with required ranking evidence still NOT EXERCISED; no confirmed numerical reward inversion is claimed.
counterexample: Plausible false-pass witness, supported at the helper level rather than by an app score: a shared volatile-memory snippet server with a SIGTERM handler that leaves its listener alive can keep every record through the claimed restart. The raw helper reproduction shows old PID 7 continuing while new PID 67 fails EADDRINUSE and the helper returns success. S22 may then award restart durability from unchanged in-memory records even though a real process restart would lose them. Its 2.0 Functional weight is 0.6*2/32.7 = approximately 0.0367 reward above the floor. This is a candidate overcredit mechanism to include in paired ranking measurements, not evidence that such a weak full app has actually outscored a stronger app. The conforming alternatives examined in the evidence did not expose a source-level false failure.
suggested_fix: Keep row 42 unmeasured until authorized configured-judge runs compare the unchanged reference with representative partial/broken apps and bind actual per-criterion, dimension and final rewards plus raw commands/logs to this input hash. Include the volatile-memory/resistant-process case. Resolve the inherited restart-helper false-success issue through the canonical harness owner, then use a new frozen candidate if shared bytes change; do not locally rewrite frozen scoring policy or claim scripted timing proves judge ordering.
